title: Potential Targets and Signaling Mechanisms of Cinnamaldehyde Enhancing Intestinal Function and Nutritional Regulation in Fat Greenling (Hexagrammos otakii).
authors: Gu, Yixin; Zhan, Yu; Guo, Yafeng; Hua, Wenyuan; Qi, Xin; Gu, Zhizhi; Cao, Shengnan; Chen, Yan; Xue, Zhuang; Wang, Wei
one_liner_zh: 该文研究肉桂醛抗肠炎机制，涉及NF-κB通路和分子对接，但核心是药物-蛋白作用而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI/物理模拟方法，仅边缘相关。
abstract: Cinnamaldehyde is an ideal feed additive with good immune enhancement and anti-inflammatory regulation effects. However, the anti-inflammatory regulation mechanism in fat greenling (Hexagrammos otakii, H. otakii) remains unclear. The nine targets of cinnamaldehyde were gathered in identified by the Traditional Chinese Medicine Systems Pharmacology database and Uniprot database, and 1,320 intestinal inflammation disease (IIF)-related proteins were screened from DrugBank, Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man (OMIM), Genecards, and Pharmacogenetics and Pharmacogenomics Knowledge Base (PHARMGKB) Databases. According to the Gene Ontology enrichment results and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes pathway results, cinnamaldehyde may regulated the responses to bacteria, lipopolysaccharide, an inflammatory cytokine, and external stimuli via the nuclear factor kappa-B (NFkappaB) signaling pathway within on inflammatory network. In addition, the protein-protein interaction analysis assisted in obtaining the closely related inflammatory regulatory proteins, including the C5a anaphylatoxin chemotactic receptor 1 (C5aR1), transcription factor p65 (RELA), prostaglandin G/H synthase 2 (PTGS2), and toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), which were confirmed as the bottleneck nodes of the network to be more deeply verified via the molecular docking. Moreover, a cinnamaldehyde feeding model was established for evaluating the anti-inflammatory effect of cinnamaldehyde in vivo. According to the current findings implied that cinnamaldehyde may play a protective role against IIF H. otakii by reducing inflammation through the C5 complement (C5)/C5aR1/interleukin-6 (IL-6) and TLR4/NFkappaB/PTGS2 pathway. The study focused on investigating the action mechanism of cinnamaldehyde on IIF through combining pharmacology and experimental verification in vivo, which provided a fresh perspective on the promoting effect of cinnamaldehyde on IIF in fish.
abstract_zh: 肉桂醛是一种理想的饲料添加剂，具有良好的免疫增强和抗炎调节作用。然而，其在脂肪绿鳍鱼（Hexagrammos otakii, H. otakii）中的抗炎调节机制尚不清楚。通过中药系统药理学数据库和Uniprot数据库收集并鉴定了肉桂醛的九个靶点，并从DrugBank、在线人类孟德尔遗传数据库（OMIM）、Genecards和药物遗传学与药物基因组学知识库（PHARMGKB）中筛选出1,320个肠道炎症疾病（IIF）相关蛋白。根据基因本体论富集结果和京都基因与基因组百科全书通路结果，肉桂醛可能通过核因子kappa-B（NFkappaB）信号通路调节对细菌、脂多糖、炎症细胞因子和外部刺激的响应，在炎症网络内发挥作用。此外，蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用分析有助于获得紧密相关的炎症调节蛋白，包括C5a过敏毒素趋化受体1（C5aR1）、转录因子p65（RELA）、前列腺素G/H合酶2（PTGS2）和Toll样受体4（TLR4），这些被确认为网络的瓶颈节点，并通过分子对接进一步验证。此外，建立了肉桂醛饲喂模型，以评估肉桂醛在体内的抗炎效果。根据当前发现，肉桂醛可能通过C5补体（C5）/C5aR1/白细胞介素-6（IL-6）和TLR4/NFkappaB/PTGS2通路减少炎症，从而对H. otakii的IIF发挥保护作用。本研究通过结合药理学和体内实验验证，重点探讨了肉桂醛对IIF的作用机制，为肉桂醛在鱼类中促进IIF的作用提供了新视角。
